evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep says 'I just confirm, you know, confirm the details here and ask you some few questions and then this should take about like ten minutes and then we'll be able to provide you an accurate estimate' — time-boxed but the promise of a dependable quote is weak, and no explicit yes-gate before proceeding.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Rep asks: 'So for this upcoming move, what are your biggest concerns and what are the most important things you'd like answers to on this, you know, or in this conversation today?' — asked before logistics probing and customer responds with detailed concern about storage units and directional placement.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raises concern about two storage units and needing direction/placement by room. Rep follows up: 'But for now, I just like to confirm so since we're talking about two storage units here...' and continues probing with 'how full the two units are,' 'what size of house last time,' 'roughly how many boxes,' and multiple clarifications on the pickup location, truck height restrictions, and parking. Concern is fully explored across multiple turns.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: Rep never summarizes or reflects back the customer's stated concerns. After the customer lists her concerns (storage units, direction/placement, professional movers), rep acknowledges with 'Mm-hmm' repeatedly but does not use a closing reflection like 'So what I'm hearing is...' or ask 'Did I get all of it?'
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Rep covers: property type (two-story house), floor level (first floor storage units, two-story destination), number of rooms (implied via three bedroom prior home), walking distance (thirty steps from truck to storage), additional rooms (office, craft shop mentioned), special considerations (11-foot height restriction on storage unit, truck must offload outside), and additional stops (two storage units). All seven logistics items addressed.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Rep asks 'roughly how many boxes are we talking about?' and customer estimates 50+, rep anchors to typical 55–65 for three-bedroom-plus-crafter household.
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Rep never asks 'Would you like us to pack your items into boxes for you?' — no packing service offer made.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep provides typical ranges: 'typical ten by twenty usually takes two movers one track between seven and a half to nine and a half hours plus the 10x10. Usually it takes four to five and a half hours.' Then personalizes: 'So in your case since you are moving from two storage units, alright, indoor storage units going to a two story house then I would estimate the move between six to seven hours.' Also personalizes pricing with crew size: 'I am thinking about sending three movers, okay? Cause with the boxes and stuff and then also, you know, moving to a two story house.' Final quote: '$2,000 or around $2,004 to $2,313' for six to seven hours with three movers.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Rep discloses fees upfront: 'The only thing outside of the hourly rate is the trip fee of $150. It's a one time fee because both addresses are out outside of the free service zone already.' Also covers 'no hidden fees of any type. No credit card fees, no stair. Well, fees.' Rep also states 'We have a two and a half hour minimum, and once we go over that minimum the time is prorated in fifteen minute increments.' Framing is present and clear.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Rep never asks 'Does that feel fair?' or equivalent. After pricing is stated, rep asks 'Yeah, though, so that, does that make sense or do you have questions or clarifications' — a different question without a pause for reflection on fairness. No 'feel fair' ask detected.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Rep states: 'finally we have the on time guarantee. So, if we can't make it in the time window that we arrange, we immediately start discounting money of your final bill and all of that is included at no extra cost.' Discount terms are clearly explained.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Rep explains: 'Our free evaluation coverage is included in the hourly rate and we provide up to $2,000 per move to repair, replace or reimburse for accidental damages.' Also states 'Unlike our competitors who either charge extra for it or offer only state mandated 60¢ per pound coverage only. But with us, we can give up the $2,000 per move.' Language confirms no deductible and no fine print — it's built into the rate. Full delivery.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: Rep does not ask 'Does that put those to rest?' or equivalent after covering the Two Promises. Rep moves directly to timing/minimum without confirming the promises resolved customer concerns. No loop closure.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Rep never asks 'What's still concerning you about this move?' or any genuine final-concerns check. The call ends with 'just give us a call if you're ready to proceed with Einstein and they'll be more than happy to assist.' No genuine final concerns prompt.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: Rep does not ask 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' — no catch-all question asked.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Rep asks 'would you like our help with your upcoming move?' but immediately provides an out: 'So I'll go ahead and send you an email after this call.' Customer responds 'I can't make that decision, I would have to leave that decision to him and that's why I asked to haven't, you know, emailed to me.' Rep accepts this without re-asking or removing the out. The 'email option' is a built-in softener.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: Rep never mentions 'rate lock' or 'no-price-change guarantee.' Pricing is quoted but no rate-lock assurance given.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Rep collects no booking details. Customer declines to book (needs to consult husband), rep offers to email the quote, and call ends without confirming date, phone, arrival window, crew size, addresses, or notes for crew. Zero booking confirmation.

top_strength: Jevic gathered exceptionally thorough logistics details across both pickup locations and the destination, identified the critical 11-foot height restriction that would have derailed the move, and provided a detailed, personalized estimate anchored to typical ranges while explicitly addressing the customer's concern about directional placement and professional movers.
coaching_note: You skipped the active-listening reflection in Section 2 (summarize and confirm concerns), never asked 'Does that feel fair?' after pricing, missed the final-concerns check and catch-all in Section 6, and accepted a built-in out ('I'll just email this') instead of holding a real yes/no ask — plan to tighten Sections 2, 4, 6, and 7 on your next call.
